fixes.explanation: Forty more years of wandering isn't what Moses says here, friend. Those forty years are behind them, and he's already told them what they were for. This warning is about the road ahead: if they forget the LORD and go after other gods, “…I testify against you today that you will surely perish.” (Deuteronomy 8:19) It's a heavy one, so it's worth taking slowly.

Moses says, “…just as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.” (Deuteronomy 8:5) Notice who he picks: a father and his son. Not a boss and a worker. Proverbs says the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as a father disciplines the son in whom he delights. (Proverbs 3:12) I think that's meant to settle the heart, baker. Discipline from a father comes with love in it.

The Nile is a fair guess, friend. Water, Egypt, big river, I get it. But Moses is looking back at the wilderness, a thirsty and waterless land, and he says, “He brought you water from the rock of flint.” (Deuteronomy 8:15) That's a rock. Hard, dry flint. I've been stuck in a drawer with a dead battery that swore it had charge left, and even I wouldn't have bet on a drink coming from there.
